intent: To demonstrate that corporate and property taxes disproportionately burden the wealthiest individuals.

units.meaning: The RICHEST group has the highest relative_value, 0.3667 (36.67%), among all entities.
accepted_routes: The richest group faces a 36.67% relative burden, the highest of all groups.
RICHEST has the top relative_value at 0.3667.
At 36.7%, the richest group's relative tax burden tops the chart.
units.visual_evidence_rule: RICHEST bar must be the tallest in the relative-value series, with 0.3667 or 36.67% visible or legible.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause 'these corporate and property taxes hit them the hardest' referencing the richest.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly identify RICHEST as having the highest relative burden?

units.meaning: The RICHEST group's relative_value (0.3667) is about 5.5 times the POOREST group's relative_value (0.0667), a 30 percentage-point gap.
accepted_routes: Richest relative burden is 5.5x the poorest.
A 30 percentage-point difference in relative burden.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both POOREST and RICHEST relative-value bars must be visible with labels or axis values allowing the ratio or difference to be derived.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause 'hit them the hardest' contrasting rich and poor.
units.reviewer_question: Is the 5.5x ratio (or 30-point gap) between richest and poorest required, or is showing both endpoints enough?

units.meaning: The two highest groups (Group 10 and RICHEST) have much larger absolute values (9.000 and 11.000) than the poorest groups (e.g., POOREST at 2.000).

basis.note: one of the lowest absolute values

accepted_routes: Group 10 and RICHEST have values of 9 and 11, far above the poorest group's 2.
The richest groups' absolute tax amounts dwarf the poorest groups' amounts.
Top two groups are 9 and 11 versus 2 for the poorest.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Bars for Group 10 and RICHEST must be visibly taller than the POOREST bar on the absolute-value axis.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause 'rich people own more things' or 'taxes hit them the hardest'.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video compare absolute values of top vs bottom groups, or is relative value sufficient?

units.meaning: Only the top two groups cross the 30% relative-value threshold: Group 10 has 0.3000 and RICHEST has 0.3667, while all other groups are at 0.1000 or below.
accepted_routes: Group 10 and RICHEST are the only groups at or above 30% relative burden.
The relative burden crosses 30% only for the two richest groups.
All groups up to Group 9 are at 10% or less; Group 10 and RICHEST exceed 30%.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A threshold marker at 0.3000 (30%) must show only Group 10 and RICHEST above it, with other bars below.
units.temporal_anchor: optional clause emphasizing the sharp jump for the wealthiest groups.
units.reviewer_question: Should the video include the 30% threshold crossing as an explicit takeaway?

units.meaning: The absolute value trend is flat at 2.000 for the poorest groups, rises to 3.000 for Groups 7-9, then jumps sharply to 9.000 for Group 10 and 11.000 for RICHEST.
accepted_routes: Values stay low then spike for the top two groups.
The distribution is heavily skewed: 2, 3, then 9 and 11.
A sharp rise at the right end of the chart.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The bar chart must display a low plateau followed by a sharp increase at Group 10 and RICHEST.
units.temporal_anchor: overall narration or the clause 'Usually rich people own more things'.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video convey the overall increasing trend and sharp top-end jump?

optional_valid: Listing every group's exact value is optional.
Highlighting Group 10 alone as the second-highest value is optional.
Showing the full ordered sequence of groups from POOREST through RICHEST is optional if the trend is clear.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claim that corporate/property taxes cause wealth inequality.
Extrapolating beyond the groups shown in the table.
Treating relative_value as a share of total (the listed relative_values sum to more than 1).
Claiming the poorest groups pay zero or negative taxes.
notes: The table has a duplicate POOREST row; treat the intended series as wealth-ordered groups. Relative_value appears to be a rate or burden, not a share of total.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
